panels.title: Worker Availability
panels.description: One lane per worker container (hostname is its container id). A deploy shows the old lane going red as a new one starts; red on the only worker is CeleryNoWorkersOnline.

panels.title: Tasks Running per Worker
panels.description: Tasks executing right now. Pinned at the worker's concurrency while the queue grows means the worker is saturated.

panels.title: Worker Utilization
panels.description: Running tasks against the worker processes consuming the queues. Near 100% for long while the queue grows means the workers need more concurrency.

panels.title: Workers & Processes per Queue
panels.description: Processes is the total concurrency consuming each queue.

panels.title: Queue Length (waiting tasks)
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a worker, per queue. Brief spikes that drain are normal; above 100 for 15 minutes fires CeleryQueueBacklog.

panels.title: Enqueued vs Started
panels.description: Tasks per minute going into the queue and being picked up. enqueued staying above started is a queue that is growing.

panels.title: Task Throughput by State
panels.description: Tasks per minute at each stage. sent is published by web and beat, the rest by the workers. received well above succeeded + failed for long means tasks are piling up or hanging.

panels.title: Started by Task
panels.description: Tasks per minute, per task: where the work comes from.

panels.title: Failure Ratio by Task

targets.expr: sum by (name) (rate(celery_task_failed_total{name=~"$task", hostname=~"$worker", queue_name=~"$queue"}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (name) (rate(celery_task_started_total{name=~"$task", hostname=~"$worker", queue_name=~"$queue"}[5m])), 0.001) * 100 > 0

panels.description: Share of each task's runs that failed, over 5 minutes. Only tasks with failures appear. 10%+ with 3 or more failures in 15 minutes fires CeleryTaskFailing.

panels.title: Retries, Rejections & Revocations
panels.description: Per task, per minute. Retries climbing usually mean a dependency (the ETL service, a calendar API, SMTP) is failing intermittently.

panels.title: Runtime Percentiles
panels.description: Completed runs across the selected tasks. Buckets reach 30 minutes (see the celery-exporter --buckets flag).

panels.title: p95 Runtime by Task

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (name, le) (rate(celery_task_runtime_bucket{name=~"$task", hostname=~"$worker", queue_name=~"$queue"}[5m])))

panels.description: A task whose line keeps rising is heading for a timeout.

targets.expr: topk(15, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (name, le) (rate(celery_task_runtime_bucket{name=~"$task", hostname=~"$worker", queue_name=~"$queue"}[1h]))))

panels.title: Worker Time by Task (last hour)
panels.description: Total seconds of worker time each task used: where the capacity goes. A cheap task run very often can outrank a slow one.

panels.title: Failures by Task & Exception (24h)
panels.description: Every failing task with the exception it raised. Empty is the goal. The full error text is in Recent Task Failures below.

panels.title: Failures by Exception
panels.description: Failures per minute by exception type, across the selected tasks. One exception spiking across many tasks points at a shared dependency rather than a bug in one task.

panels.title: Recent Task Failures
panels.description: The exception each failed task raised, from the worker log. Follows the Task filter. Expand a line for the traceback.

panels.title: Beat: Tasks Dispatched
panels.description: Periodic tasks celery beat sent per minute, from its log. A flat zero where there used to be a steady pattern means beat has stopped scheduling. Beat publishes no heartbeat of its own; its container healthcheck (schedule file freshness) is the other signal, on the right.

panels.title: Celery Container Health
panels.description: Docker healthchecks of the worker (inspect ping) and beat (schedule file written in the last 15 minutes).

panels.title: Beat Log
panels.description: Everything beat logs: dispatches, schedule changes, and errors reaching the broker.
